title: Use whole-coset isolation to remove encoder-image testing under the decoding promise
statement: Assume the affine construction outputs codewords each isolated from EVERY other same-coset word within edit distance2t. If y is within t edits of Enc(u), every same-coset x-prime within t of y obeys d(Enc(u),x-prime)<=2t and hence equals Enc(u). Thus a syndrome-constrained reconstruction routine need not test encoder-image membership on genuine encoded transmissions; invert signed-prefix indexing to recover u. Uniform polynomial exact signed-witness aggregation and suitable polynomial reconstruction would SUFFICE for setup/encoding/decoding, but neither is constructed. Arbitrary-affine aggregation and whole-coset reconstruction on all off-promise inputs can be stronger than an actual code needs; they are not proven necessary. Ordinary pairwise codebook distance alone does not justify whole-coset uniqueness.
